clue.text: Marks on wood of old instrument'

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: a shaw is an old word for a small wood or thicket
M is the abbreviation for marks, the former German currency

explanation.surface: Someone notices scratches on the wooden body of an antique musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The shawm was a medieval double-reed woodwind, forerunner of the oboe.

clue.text: Leading light in flower show .

definitions.meaning: the star that guided the Magi to the manger, a light that led
a white-flowered bulbous plant of the lily family

explanation.surface: The star attraction at a horticultural show.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the guiding star of the Nativity story and a white-starred wild bulb carry this name.

clue.text: Don Quixote's so long!

parts.note: Cervantes's Spanish knight would say goodbye in Spanish; the surface pretends to complain about the novel's length

explanation.surface: A grumble that the novel Don Quixote goes on far too long.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Spanish farewell, the equivalent of goodbye or so long.

clue.text: Dangerous play? Don't mention it!

definitions.meaning: a drama thought by theatre folk to bring bad luck
actors superstitiously refuse to name this play inside a theatre, calling it the Scottish Play

explanation.surface: A risky manoeuvre, and a polite reply waving away thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Scottish tragedy is held unlucky, so actors avoid saying its title backstage.

clue.text: Fear bound to disappear before too long?

definitions.text: Fear bound to disappear before too long?

parts.words: Fear bound to disappear before too long?
parts.note: a dread of novelty, which by nature wears off as anything new soon stops being new

explanation.surface: A reassurance that some anxiety will soon pass.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the dread of anything new, and novelty is always short-lived.

clue.text: Intelligence shown by them? On the contrary

definitions.text: Intelligence shown by them? On the contrary

parts.words: Intelligence shown by them? On the contrary
parts.note: the French word for us is also English slang for common sense, so the wit belongs not to them but to us

explanation.surface: A dismissive aside about the cleverness of other people.
explanation.walkthrough: The French pronoun for 'we/us' is the contrary of 'them', and the same word is British slang for good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from Greek, it is British informal for practical common sense.

clue.text: Piled up, catching front of car? Doing little damage

indicators.note: one piece catching another holds it inside

parts.note: things piled up are on the heap

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Cars piled up in a crash, yet barely scratched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' puts C, the first letter of 'car', inside ON THE HEAP; the definition means doing little damage to one's purse.
explanation.definitionFit: Done cheaply, something costs little, so it is light on the wallet.

clue.text: Smell, one that's upset staff in cigar store

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: A whiff in a tobacconist's, and someone has knocked over a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A humidor is a humidified box or room for keeping cigars.

clue.text: Get yellow container opened

parts.note: a bottle holds liquid
flowers that have opened are out

explanation.surface: Someone fetches a yellow jar and takes the lid off.
explanation.walkthrough: Yellow means cowardly; BOTTLE OUT is British slang for losing one's nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose courage and withdraw is to turn cowardly.

clue.text: Material for statesman's speech?

parts.note: a statesman read as a man from the States, whose speech is the variety of the language spoken there

explanation.surface: A politician's speechwriter looks for content.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the form of the language used in the USA, the native tongue of any American.

clue.text: 'A trap set by royal supporters in battle

parts.note: a gin is a snare for animals
a court is the retinue around a monarch

explanation.surface: An ambush laid by the king's followers in a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Agincourt was Henry V's victory over the French in 1415.

clue.text: The writer crosses over the top of site of castle

indicators.note: the word crosses another by spanning it, so the letters sit either side

parts.note: the writer of a clue refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: An author climbs over the top of a castle's ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: A motte is the earthen mound on which a Norman castle keep was built.

clue.text: Succeeded in external legal removal

indicators.note: the letter goes into the middle of the word for external

parts.note: outer means on the outside
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A court succeeds in having someone ejected from outside.
explanation.definitionFit: In law an ouster is a wrongful dispossession or expulsion from property.

clue.text: Capital hard to invest in modern store

parts.note: new means modern

indicators.note: investing one thing in another puts it inside, so the letter goes into the shop

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food store
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Money to sink into a new shop venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to invest in' puts H inside DELI.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the seat of India's government.

clue.text: Leaves in this ship for fleet movement

definitions.text: Leaves in this ship for fleet movement

parts.words: Leaves in this ship for fleet movement
parts.note: leaves read as dried leaves for brewing carried aboard a fast sailing vessel, fleet meaning swift rather than naval

explanation.surface: A vessel departs to join a naval fleet's manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: These fast nineteenth-century sailing ships raced cargoes of tea from China.

clue.text: Tip to bet on's sound?.He's doubly confused

indicators.note: the clue says the word for bet on is heard, not spelt

parts.note: to back a horse is to bet on it

indicators.note: confused means the letters are mixed up
doubly means the word he's is taken twice

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice on a wager, and a man in a muddle twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly' gives HESHES and 'confused' rearranges it to SHEESH.
explanation.definitionFit: Baksheesh is a gratuity or small bribe in the Middle East.

clue.text: Problem with informer in plant

parts.note: a knot is a tangled problem
a grass is British slang for a police informer

explanation.surface: Trouble with a snitch planted inside an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotgrass is a common weed of the dock family.

clue.text: Judge a port, at first, as wine

indicators.note: the port is placed first, before the other pieces

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A magistrate takes port as an aperitif and wine afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine from northern Spain.

clue.text: Bunch of communists producing moderate movements

definitions.meaning: a horse's gait between walking and galloping

explanation.surface: A gang of Reds bringing in middling reforms.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both slang for followers of Trotsky and the plural of a horse's jogging pace.

clue.text: Girl and dog jump over ice

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally
a chow is a Chinese breed of dog

explanation.surface: A girl and her dog leap across a frozen pond.
explanation.definitionFit: A salchow is a figure-skating leap named after its Swedish inventor.

clue.text: Queen of puddings?

parts.note: George III's queen shares her name with a fruit dessert in a bread or sponge case

explanation.surface: Queen of puddings is a classic British dessert; the clue asks who rules them.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlotte is a baked fruit pudding, and Charlotte was the wife of George III.

clue.text: Desire dance, but this ball's not good enough

parts.note: to long is to desire
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Yearning for a dance, but the ball is a disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a long hop is a short-pitched, easily hit delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket delivery pitched far too short is a poor one, easily hit for runs.

clue.text: Support advocate' initially arranged?

parts.note: state-funded help with lawyers' fees, sorted out at the start so that a client can be represented

explanation.surface: A barrister's backing was set up from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: It is public funding for legal advice and representation.

clue.text: Going round corner without start or finish

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a car going round a corner is bending

explanation.surface: A driver takes the bend with neither a beginning nor an end.
explanation.definitionFit: A conclusion is where something finishes.

clue.text: That's one way to modify diets

indicators.note: modifying the letters means changing their order

explanation.surface: A recommendation for changing what one eats.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, shortened to i.e., means that is.

clue.text: As king, I had the means to distribute power

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A monarch boasts of his ways of sharing out authority.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Grid is Britain's electricity transmission network.
explanation.definitionFit: The network of cables carries electricity across the country.

clue.text: Where we three met, in the Athenaeum

indicators.note: the answer sits in the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: The three of us met at a London gentlemen's club, the Athenaeum.
explanation.walkthrough: The three witches of Macbeth meet on a blasted heath.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's witches gather on open moorland.

clue.text: Rash piece to move in board game

indicators.note: moving the letters means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A careless chess piece is about to be moved.
explanation.definitionFit: Parcheesi is the American version of the Indian board game pachisi.

clue.text: Female competitor beating all the others in many races

definitions.text: Female competitor beating all the others in many races

parts.words: Female competitor beating all the others in many races
parts.note: races read as ethnic groups, not sprints: the winner of an international beauty contest

explanation.surface: A woman athlete wins numerous running events.
explanation.definitionFit: The title goes to the winner of an international beauty pageant.

clue.text: Way in which Conservative's protected beauty spot

indicators.note: the way surrounds the letter, protecting it

parts.note: a path is a way
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A path where the Tory party guards a scenic place.
explanation.walkthrough: A patch is a small black facial patch once worn as a beauty spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgian fashion wore small silk patches on the face as artificial beauty marks.
